To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the planning technique can provide a general approach to feedback in interactive learning environment.

(1) the use of planning techniques to provide appropriate feedback is feasible, (2) planning techniques can be used to provide feedback in a wide range of domains, and (3) the use of a planning formulation that incorporates a representation of the user's goals is particularly effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for the design and implementation of intelligent tutors in procedural domains.
the design of a general framework for representing procedural domains, tasks, and feedback within an interactive learning environment.
the representation and manipulation of domain and task knowledge in an interactive learning system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the work reported in this paper has demonstrated that a planning-based approach to task analysis and representation can provide an effective and efficient means of representing tasks in a range of domains.
the work reported here is a step towards the goal of providing an interactive learning environment which is capable of giving suitable feedback for a wide range of procedural domains.
a planning based approach is suitable for the representation of procedural domains and the generation of appropriate feedback in interactive learning systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the planning formalism has enabled us to provide a simple and elegant representation of the domain and tasks.
the approach described in this paper is an effective and economical method for providing suitable feedback in a wide range of interactive learning environments.
we have shown how to use a planning system for the purpose of providing feedback in an interactive environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a planning-based approach to representing tasks in a domain is an effective way to provide a rich set of feedback options to a learner.
it is possible, in principle, to represent the operation of a device in terms of the planning formalism, and to use that representation to provide feedback in a tutoring environment.
it is possible to represent procedural tasks in a planning formalism, and to use the resulting representations in a tutoring system.
